readings.title: The Congregation Rebels
readings.subtitle: Israel Despises the Promised Land
readings.text: [Numbers 14:1] Then all the congregation lifted up their voices and cried, and the people wept that night. [2] And all the children of Yisra’ěl grumbled against Mosheh and against Aharon, and all the congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Mitsrayim! Or if only we had died in this wilderness! [3] “And why is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> bringing us to this land to fall by the sword, that our wives and children should become a prey? Would it not be better for us to turn back to Mitsrayim?” [4] And they said to each other, “Let us appoint a leader, and let us turn back to Mitsrayim.” [5] Then Mosheh and Aharon fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl. [6] And Yehoshua son of Nun, and Kalěḇ son of Yephunneh, who were among those who had spied out <dn>את</dn> the land, tore their garments, [7] and they spoke to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, “The land we passed through to spy out is an exceedingly good land. [8] “If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has delighted in us, then <dn>He</dn> shall bring us into this land and give it to us, ‘a land which is flowing with milk and honey.’ [9] “Only, do not rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor fear <dn>את</dn> the people of the land, for they are our bread. Their defence has turned away from them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with us. Do not fear them.” [10] But all the congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared in the Tent of Appointment before all the children of Yisra’ěl. [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“How long shall <dn>I</dn> be scorned by these people? And how long shall <dn>I</dn> not be trusted by them, with all the signs which <dn>I</dn> have done in their midst?</dq> [12] <dq>“Let <dn>Me</dn> strike them with the pestilence and disinherit them, and make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”</dq>

readings.title: The Intercession of Moses
readings.subtitle: Pardon and the Decree of Exile
readings.text: [Numbers 14:13] And Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Then the Mitsrites shall hear it, for by <dn>Your</dn> power <dn>You</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> these people up from their midst, [14] and they shall say to the inhabitants of this land they have heard that <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are in the midst of these people, that <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are seen eye to eye and that <dn>Your</dn> cloud stands above them, and <dn>You</dn> go before them in a column of cloud by day and in a column of fire by night. [15] “Now if <dn>You</dn> shall kill <dn>את</dn> these people as one man, then the nations which have heard of <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> report shall speak, saying, [16] Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not able to bring <dn>את</dn> this people to the land which <dn>He</dn> swore to give them, therefore <dn>He</dn> slew them in the wilderness.’ [17] “And now, I pray, let the power of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be great, as <dn>You</dn> have spoken, saying, [18] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is patient and of great loving-commitment, forgiving crookedness and transgression, but by no means leaving unpunished; visiting the crookedness of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation.’ [19] “Please forgive the crookedness of this people, according to the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment, as <dn>You</dn> have forgiven this people, from Mitsrayim even until now.” [20] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall forgive, according to your word,</dq> [21] <dq>but truly, as <dn>I</dn> live and all <dn>את</dn> the earth is filled with the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [22] <dq>for none of these men who have seen <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> esteem and <dn>את</dn> the signs which <dn>I</dn> did in Mitsrayim and in the wilderness, and have tried <dn>Me</dn> now these ten times, and have disobeyed <dn>My</dn> voice,</dq> [23] <dq>shall see <dn>את</dn> the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to their fathers, nor any of those who scorned <dn>Me</dn> see it.</dq> [24] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> servant Kalěḇ, because he has a different spirit in him and has followed <dn>Me</dn> completely, <dn>I</dn> shall bring into the land where he went, and his seed shall inherit it.</dq> [25] <dq>“Since the Amalěqites and the Kena‛anites are dwelling in the valley, turn back tomorrow and set out into the wilderness by the Way of the Sea of Reeds.”</dq>

readings.title: The Forty-Year Sentence
readings.subtitle: The Presumptuous Defeat at Hormah
readings.text: [Numbers 14:26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, and to Aharon, saying, [27] <dq>“How long shall this evil congregation have this grumbling against <dn>Me</dn>? <dn>I</dn> have heard the grumblings which the children of Yisra’ěl are grumbling against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“Say to them, ‘As <dn>I</dn> live,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>’as you have spoken in <dn>My</dn> hearing, so <dn>I</dn> do to you:</dq> [29] <dq>The carcasses of you who have grumbled against <dn>Me</dn> are going to fall in this wilderness, all of you who were registered, according to your entire number, from twenty years old and above.</dq> [30] <dq>None of you except Kalěḇ son of Yephunneh, and Yehoshua son of Nun, shall enter the land which <dn>I</dn> swore <dn>I</dn> would make you dwell in.</dq> [31] <dq>But your little ones, whom you said would become a prey, <dn>I</dn> shall bring in, and they shall know <dn>את</dn> the land which you have rejected.</dq> [32] <dq>But as for you, your carcasses are going to fall in this wilderness.</dq> [33] <dq>And your sons shall be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear <dn>את</dn> your whorings, until your carcasses are consumed in the wilderness.</dq> [34] <dq>According to the number of the days in which you spied out <dn>את</dn> the land, forty days – a day for a year, a day for a year – you are to bear <dn>את</dn> your crookednesses forty years, and you shall know <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> breaking off.</dq> [35] <dq><dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have spoken, <dn>I</dn> shall do this to all this evil congregation who are meeting against <dn>Me</dn>: In this wilderness they are consumed, and there they die.’ ”</dq> [36] And the men whom Mosheh sent to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land, who returned and made all the congregation grumble against him by bringing an evil report of the land, [37] even those men who brought the evil report about the land, died by the plague before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [38] Of those men who went to spy out <dn>את</dn> the land, only Yehoshua son of Nun, and Kalěḇ son of Yephunneh remained alive. [39] And when Mosheh spoke <dn>את</dn> these words to all the children of Yisra’ěl, the people mourned greatly. [40] And they rose up early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “See, we have indeed sinned, but we shall go up to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken of!” [41] But Mosheh said, “Why do you now transgress the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, since it does not prosper? [42] “Do not go up, lest you be smitten by your enemies, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not in your midst. [43] “Because the Amalěqites and the Kena‛anites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> ,<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not with you.” [44] But they presumed to go up to the mountaintop, but neither the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> nor Mosheh left the camp. [45] So the Amalěqites and the Kena‛anites who dwelt in that mountain came down and struck them, and beat them down, even to Ḥormah.

readings.title: Offerings of Atonement
readings.subtitle: Laws for the Native and the Stranger
readings.text: [Numbers 15:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘When you have come into the land of your dwellings, which <dn>I</dn> am giving you,</dq> [3] <dq>and you make an offering by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, an ascending offering or a slaughtering, to accomplish a vow or as a voluntary offering or in your appointed times, to make a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, from the herd or the flock,</dq> [4] <dq>then he who brings near <dn>את</dn> his offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall bring near a grain offering of one-tenth of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil,</dq> [5] <dq>and one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering you prepare with the ascending offering or the slaughtering, for each lamb.</dq> [6] <dq>Or for a ram you prepare as a grain offering two-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil,</dq> [7] <dq>and as a drink offering you bring one-third of a hin of wine as a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>And when you prepare a young bull as an ascending offering, or as a slaughtering to accomplish a vow, or as a peace offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [9] <dq>then shall be brought with the young bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,</dq> [10] <dq>and bring as the drink offering half a hin of wine as an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [11] <dq>This is what is done for each young bull, for each ram, or for each lamb or young goat.</dq> [12] <dq>According to the number that you prepare, so you do for each one according to their number.</dq> [13] <dq>Let all who are native do so with them, in bringing near an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [14] <dq>And when a stranger sojourns with you, or whoever is among you throughout your generations, and would make an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as you do, so he does.</dq> [15] <dq>One law is for you of the assembly and for the stranger who sojourns with you – a law forever throughout your generations. As you are, so is the stranger before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [16] <dq>One Torah and one right-ruling is for you and for the stranger who sojourns with you.’ ”</dq> [17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [18] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land to which <dn>I</dn> bring you,</dq> [19] <dq>then it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land, that you present a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [20] <dq>Present a cake of the first of your dough as a contribution – as a contribution of the threshing-floor you present it.</dq> [21] <dq>Of the first of your dough you are to give to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> a contribution throughout your generations.</dq> [22] <dq>And when you sin by mistake, and do not do <dn>את</dn> all these commands which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken to Mosheh,</dq> [23] <dq><dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded you by the hand of Mosheh, from the day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave command and onward throughout your generations,</dq> [24] <dq>then it shall be, if it is done by mistake, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall prepare one young bull as an ascending offering, as a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with its grain offering and its drink offering, according to the right-ruling, and one male goat as a sin offering.</dq> [25] <dq>Then the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl, and it shall be forgiven them, for it was by mistake. And they shall bring their offering, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and their sin offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for their mistake.</dq> [26] <dq>And it shall be forgiven all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl and the stranger who sojourns in their midst, because all the people did it by mistake.</dq> [27] <dq>And if a being sins by mistake, then he shall bring a female goat a year old as a sin offering.</dq> [28] <dq>And the priest shall make atonement for the being who strays by mistake, when he sins by mistake before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [29] <dq>For him who does whatever by mistake there is one Torah, both for him who is native among the children of Yisra’ěl and for the stranger who sojourns in their midst.</dq> [30] <dq>But the being who does whatever defiantly, whether he is native or a stranger, he reviles <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and that being shall be cut off from among his people.</dq> [31] <dq>Because he has despised the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and has broken <dn>His</dn> command, that being shall certainly be cut off, his crookedness is upon him.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Sabbath Breaker
readings.subtitle: Judgment Outside the Camp
readings.text: [Numbers 15:32] And while the children of Yisra’ěl were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. [33] And those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Mosheh and to Aharon, and to all the congregation. [34] And they put him in under guard, because it had not been declared what should be done to him. [35] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“The man shall certainly be put to death, all the congregation stoning him with stones outside the camp.”</dq> [36] And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh, and he died.

readings.title: The Command of the Tzitzit
readings.subtitle: Remembering the Torah of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Numbers 15:37] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [38] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and you shall say to them to make tzitzit on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord in the tzitzit of the corners.</dq> [39] <dq>“And it shall be to you for a tzitzit, and you shall see it, and shall remember <dn>את</dn> all the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and shall do them, and not search after your own heart and your own eyes after which you went whoring,</dq> [40] <dq>so that you remember, and shall do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> commands, and be set-apart unto your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [41] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.”</dq>
